title: Normalizing State
description: Learn how to structure state for efficient updates using normalized data structures.

data.text: When building real applications, you often deal with collections of data like users, posts, comments, or products. How you structure this data in your Redux store has a huge impact on how easy it is to update and retrieve.

**Normalizing state** means storing entities in a flat object keyed by their unique ID, similar to how a database stores records. Instead of nested arrays and objects, each entity type gets its own table with IDs as keys. This approach makes updates efficient and consistent across your application.

Imagine you have a social media app with users, posts, and comments. A common beginner mistake is to nest this data deeply, like storing comments inside posts, and posts inside users. This creates several problems.

cards.title: Nested State
cards.content:
Hard to update related entities
Redundant data duplication
Slow lookups with deep nesting
Complex immutability updates
Difficult to cache efficiently

cards.title: Normalized State
cards.content:
Single source of truth
Easy entity updates by ID
Fast O(1) lookups
Simple immutability patterns
Reusable across components

data.text: In normalized state, entities reference each other by ID rather than containing each other. Think of it like a graph where each node is an entity and connections are just ID references.

data.caption: Normalized entity relationships

rows: Each entity type (users, posts) gets its own normalized object
Use entity IDs as keys for O(1) lookups
Maintain order with an array of all IDs
Store references as IDs, not nested objects
Each piece of data lives in exactly one place
User name only in users table
Convert nested arrays to ID arrays

data.text: You can normalize data manually or use helper functions. The key is to transform an array of entities into an object keyed by ID plus an array of IDs for ordering.

data.title: Manual Normalization

data.text: One of the biggest benefits of normalized state is how easy it becomes to update a single entity. You only need to know the entity ID; no traversing through nested objects.

data.title: Updating Normalized State
Redux Toolkit Helper
data.text: Redux Toolkit's `createEntityAdapter` automates all these normalization patterns and provides pre-built reducers and selectors.

While you store data in normalized form, you often need to display denormalized data in your components. This is where selectors come in handy. Selectors can reconstruct the nested view you need from the flat normalized state.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Normalize state by storing entities in objects keyed by ID
Avoid deeply nested structures that are hard to update
Reference entities by ID rather than embedding objects
Maintain separate allIds arrays for ordering
Use selectors to denormalize data for display
Redux Toolkit's entity adapter automates these patterns
data.takeaway: Normalized state is more efficient, easier to update, and scales better as your application grows.
